title: scrumia-tdd — ScrumIA
meta_description: scrumia-tdd: a ScrumIA module — the TDD cycle situated for an agent, mock boundary, three test levels, AC-to-test.
tagline: One named point of the implementation contract: how we test.
responsibilities: Refines a single question the implementation module leaves open — the red-green-refactor cycle operationalised for an agent, where the mock boundary sits, which of the three levels — unit, integration, end-to-end — an invariant belongs to, and how an acceptance criterion maps to a test that can actually fail at the lowest level where it could.
refusals: It does not own the stack, the file structure or the design principles — and where it disagrees with the implementation module, the implementation module wins. It carries no test command of its own, and sets no coverage threshold: the per-level commands are the project's, and the coverage union is a map of what no level reaches, never a gate.
philosophy: Assumes a failing test is the cheapest specification you can write. Costs a slower first pass, paid back only if the code outlives the sprint that produced it.
